data.narrative:
Simbe Robotics is a Series C-stage robotics and manufacturing company that has raised over $100M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comparable set spanning 1 public company and 8 private peers, with primary comparables including Hadrian ($1.6B), Agile Robots ($1.0B), and Nimble Robotics ($1.0B)—all at Series C stage within the same sector.

Two triangulation methods were applied. The stage-progression method uses the $100M total raised as a proxy base value and applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical for Series C advancement, implying a valuation of $170M. The peer-median method anchors to three same-sector, same-stage comparables with a median valuation of $1.0B and a range spanning $1.0B to $1.6B, implying $1.0B. The divergence between these methods reflects differences in growth trajectory assumptions and peer selection.

Triangulation across both methods yields a valuation range of $144M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median estimate of $585M. The substantial spread reflects material uncertainty around Simbe's revenue scale, customer concentration, and competitive positioning relative to better-capitalized peers. Stage-progression methodology suggests more conservative valuation anchors, while peer-median comparables point toward higher valuations consistent with the broader robotics funding environment. Resolution of this range depends critically on revenue traction, customer retention metrics, and capital efficiency relative to the peer set.
